items.title: Allow users to disable PEP 714
items.reason: Direct downstream report: Pixi rewrites files.pythonhosted.org URLs to a mirror that returns 404 for an advertised .whl.metadata file. Its comments distinguish this from using a mirror's own index and explicitly propose upstreaming the small uv-client builder-setting patch. It tracks Pixi integration, not an existing uv implementation request.

items.title: [功能请求] 为 pypi 镜像实现 PEP 658 和 PEP 714，在 API 中提供包元数据
items.reason: Tracks PEP 658/714 support in the mirror used by the reproduction. Comments initially report deployment, then clarify that the deployment was rolled back; the later missing-sidecar report tuna/issues#2606 confirms that history. This is the server-side capability, distinct from the requested uv-client override.

items.title: Feature Request: Add option to disable lazy wheel (Range requests) for misconfigured servers returning Content-Length: 0 in HEAD response
items.reason: Adjacent precedent for an explicit metadata-fetching compatibility bypass: maintainers declined a switch to work around incorrect server headers, citing maintenance and performance costs. It concerns HTTP range extraction when PEP 658 metadata is absent, whereas this request skips advertised standalone metadata; it is not a duplicate or a decision on this specific API.

related.search_scope: Searched astral-sh/uv open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged PRs with authenticated gh. Literal searches covered PEP 714/658, core-metadata, dist-info-metadata, .whl.metadata, 404 Not Found, use_dist_info_metadata, and disable-pep714. Separate capability and symptom searches used disable, bypass, ignore, fallback, standalone metadata, sidecar, mirrors, and missing metadata, without package/version/platform restrictions. Inspected candidate bodies and comments, the reporter's patch, and the Pixi-to-TUNA reference chain. PR keyword searches returned no candidates; issue timelines exposed merged historical fixes that were inspected. Ruled out astral-sh/uv#3689 and fixes astral-sh/uv#3697 and astral-sh/uv#3698 (PEP 714 field-name support), astral-sh/uv#12383 and astral-sh/uv#12384 (URL fragments), and astral-sh/uv#18998 (range detection). None implements this override or establishes a regression.

type_reason: The request adds an explicit uv-client control to ignore advertised PEP 658/714 metadata for Pixi's URL-rewriting mirrors. Source confirms uv already reads metadata from wheels when sidecars are not advertised, and propagates failures when advertised sidecars cannot be fetched. The supplied failure involves inconsistent index/mirror capabilities, not established incorrect handling of a conforming index. No existing uv issue or PR was found tracking this override, and no uv regression was established; the downstream Pixi and mirror issues have separate implementation scopes.
summary: prefix-dev/pixi#7479 contains the direct reproduction and patch discussion; tuna/issues#1775 tracks mirror-side support. astral-sh/uv#17943 is a related but distinct declined compatibility switch. No existing uv duplicate or implementing PR was found.
draft_response:
uv already supports indexes without PEP 658/714: when no standalone metadata is advertised, it reads metadata from the wheel. In prefix-dev/pixi#7479, the index advertises metadata files but Pixi rewrites their URLs to a mirror that does not serve them, so the fetch fails.

Your patch proposes a new uv-client builder setting to override that advertisement. The next step is a maintainer decision on that API and its scope; there is no existing bypass switch. For now, using a mirror that serves the advertised metadata files avoids this mismatch.
